target_customer: Men, especially golfers and corporate buyers, who struggle to find well-fitting polos and shirts
problem: Standard sizes differ by brand, so many men shop several stores to find a shirt that fits.
business_model: E-commerce of made-to-order apparel with a free home try-on sample program

founders.name: Jonathan Tang
founders.background_notes: Sources reviewed give no further background.

technical_complexity.rationale: A fit quiz and recommendation algorithm plus order customization on top of contract manufacturing; the hard parts were operations and supply chain, not software.

defensibility.rationale: Saved fit profiles gave mild lock-in, but competitors already sold custom shirts and polos were easy to copy.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent bought it. A menswear brand, Stantt, acquired it in July 2026.

market_need_then: Fit pain was common enough that TechCrunch covered the home try-on model in 2012 and 2013, targeting golfers and corporate clients; no spend data found.

branding.name_origin: Vastrm is described on the YC page as a Sanskrit word for cloth, chosen by the founder.
branding.domain_note: vastrm.com later redirects to stantt.com after the 2026 acquisition.

identity.voice_and_tone: Fit-focused, product-first copy on the YC page

branding.brand_signature: Home try-on polos with a saved fit profile
branding.community_and_virality: TechCrunch ran a hands-on review in September 2013; no merch or community found.

brand_strength.rationale: Niche press (two TechCrunch pieces) and a distinctive but hard-to-spell name; no evidence of broad awareness.

outcome_analysis: Vastrm sold customized polos with a home try-on program after the Summer 2012 batch and survived for over a decade, ending with an acquisition by Stantt in July 2026, where Dealroom describes it as a premium knitwear label. Deal terms and rounds are not public in verified sources, so it is unclear whether this was a strong or soft outcome; the long life suggests a small, capital-light business.
notes: Site vastrm.com redirects to stantt.com (fetch of the redirect target not performed). Unverified funding: SeedTable lists a $1.0M seed in August 2013 (investor Quest Venture Partners visible) and PitchBook and CB Insights estimate about $1.65M total; all single aggregators, so no round is recorded. Dealroom dates founding to 2013 and PitchBook lists the sale as 21 July 2026 against Dealroom's 23 July 2026. The YC page says the founder is Jonathan Tang but also refers to Tang and Jonathan separately; treated as one person. Completeness pass: the 1.0M seed of 2013-08 rests on Seedtable (Finsmes also reports a 1M seed, page not readable) and the 650K Seed II of 2014-10-22 on CB Insights alone, which totals 1.67M over four rounds; totals conflict (1.0M, 1.65M, 1.67M) and two rounds are unaccounted for.
